I am 57, I have farmed these 5 mu in Quzhou for 30 years. My husband and son work part-time in town, so I manage most of the field work myself with help at harvest. I went to middle school, so I can read fertilizer bags and calculate costs, but I still trust what I see working in my neighbors' fields more than anything on paper.

For my wheat, I plant the whole 5 mu in October. Last year I used an improved variety — Lumai — and got about 1000 jin per mu. This year I will plant the same seed, about 30 jin per mu. Before sowing, I rotary-till the field. For the base fertilizer, I put down one bag of compound fertilizer per mu. The dealer sells a 15-15-15 blend in 50 kg bags, so that is 50 kg per mu. Then in March, when the wheat turns green and starts to grow fast, I spread 20 kg of urea per mu as a topdressing. That gives me about 18 kg of nitrogen per mu total, and 7 to 8 kg each of phosphorus and potassium. I have a well, so I irrigate three times: once in winter if the soil is too dry, once at jointing stage, and once at heading. I spray herbicide once after the wheat comes up, and if I see aphids or rust, I spray one more time. I expect around 500 kg per mu if the spring is not too dry.

For summer maize, I plant the same 5 mu right after wheat harvest in early June. I use hybrid seed — last year I used Denghai 605 and it did well, so I will buy it again, about 1.2 packages per mu. I do not till for maize; I use no-tillage direct seeding with the machine. At sowing, I put down 40 kg per mu of compound fertilizer, the 28-6-6 kind that the dealer recommends for maize. I do not topdress — once is enough for summer maize because the season is short and hot. That gives me about 14 kg nitrogen, 3 kg phosphorus, and 3 kg potassium per mu. I irrigate twice: once at the big trumpet stage and once during grain filling, because summer rain is not reliable. I spray herbicide once when the maize is small, and insecticide twice — once for corn borer and once for armyworm if they show up. I expect about 500 kg per mu.

Why these amounts? Because that is what I did last year, and my yield was decent. The fertilizer costs a lot — over 200 yuan per mu for wheat and 150 for maize — but if I cut back, I might lose 100 jin or more, and that is worse than wasting a little fertilizer. My neighbor across the road uses almost the same rates, and his crops always look good. I thought about trying slow-release fertilizer last year, but it costs more and I was not sure, so I stayed with what I know.
